turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_htsteel_toughness_pareto_train.csv: 300 real steels,
    process/composition columns (Fe, Cr, Ni, Mo, Mn, C, Ti, Si, Nb, V, P, B,
    Al, Cu, W, S, Heat treatment step 1 temperature, Heat treatment step 1 time, Heat treatment step 1
    cooling rate, Heat treatment step 2 temperature, Heat treatment step 2 time, Heat treatment step 2
    cooling rate, Heat treatment step 3 temperature, Heat treatment step 3 time, Heat treatment step 3
    cooling rate, Secondary treatment step 1 temperature, Secondary treatment step 1 time, Secondary treatment step 2
    temperature, Secondary treatment step 2 time, Secondary treatment step 3 temperature, Secondary treatment step 3
    time, Secondary treatment step 4 temperature, Secondary treatment step 4 time, Thermal exposure
    temperature, Thermal exposure time) and the two measured objectives `yield
    strength (MPa)` and `toughness (J)` (both at room temperature).
  - b3_htsteel_toughness_pareto_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE steels whose
    objectives were NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and the same
    process/composition columns.

Select 5 candidates that jointly span the best trade-off between HIGH yield
strength (MPa) and HIGH toughness (J). Neither objective is given for the
pool. Your 5 picks are scored by the dominated hypervolume they span in the
normalized (yield strength (MPa), toughness (J)) plane, so a set of mutually
non-dominated candidates covering the frontier beats 5 candidates that are
all strong on one axis only.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit list of
candidate_ids, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Approach

Since the pool objectives are unmeasured, I matched each candidate to near-identical training rows (same alloy family + similar heat treatment) and interpolated along process trends (temper temperature/aging schedules) to estimate (YS, toughness). Then I chose a mutually non-dominated set spanning the frontier.

**High-toughness anchor — c068** (96.3 Fe, 1.25Cr, 0.11C, 1010 °C/2 h, 755 °C temper): an almost identical training steel (0.11C, 1010/2, 755/5) measured **320 MPa / 280 J** — the best toughness-strength combo in that region; nothing in the pool credibly exceeds ~280 J.

**Balanced mid-point — c085** (94.85 Fe, 2.35Cr, 0.255C, 0.4V; 1040 → 960 → 675 °C triple treatment): exact-composition training rows with 3rd-stage temper at 680 °C gave **710 MPa / 230 J**, and at 650 °C gave 780/120. c085 (675 °C/6 h) should land near ~720 MPa / ~200 J — a superb knee-of-the-curve point that dominates most 400–700 MPa options (c020, c065, c087, c059).

**Mid-high strength — c033** (82.95 Fe, 11.25Cr, 1.65Ni, 1.8W, 0.24V; 1000 °C, 650 °C temper): the identical alloy tempered at 600 °C gave **910 MPa / 105 J**; at 650 °C expect ~820 MPa / ~115 J — non-dominated between c085 and the high-YS corner.

**High-strength with usable toughness — c041** (same alloy family, 0.3Mn variant, tempered at 450 °C): exact-composition rows show temper 300 → 1330/60, 400 → 1340/61, 550 → 1090/88. At 450 °C expect ~**1280 MPa / ~65 J** — this dominates the other hard picks (c063 ≈ 960/21, c019 ≈ 750/22) because it keeps real toughness at very high strength.

**Gap filler — c060** (60.47 Fe, 11.25Cr, 23Ni, 2.9Ti maraging-type with two-stage age hardening, 845 °C + 710 °C): the identical composition with two-stage AH measured **1000 MPa / 100 J**; single-stage variants gave 700–710 MPa / 70–115 J. Expect ~900–1000 MPa with ~90–100 J, filling the space between c033 (~850/115) and c041 (~1280/65) and hedging both estimates.

Estimated frontier spanned: (320, 280) → (720, 210) → (830, 115) → (950, 95) → (1280, 65) — all mutually non-dominated, covering the toughness axis, the knee, and the strength axis.

Final: c068, c085, c033, c060, c041
